raised: The page explains what products are but not what they do for your money: returns, costs, risk or who they suit
The last line of 'two parts' points to product pages the reader hasn't seen
'Where to start' has too few lines, with nothing for someone close to retirement
Unclear how the renewing money-market fund differs from a regular one
The retirement cards don't help the reader tell which fund they are in
The do-it-yourself section (self-managed, foreign broker) is not for them
The 'what the money is invested in' cards are mostly confusing
The 'what the site doesn't cover yet' box doesn't say what is missing
Differences between the index cards are lost on the reader
מק"מ appears twice, once as a place money is held and once as an investment, so which is it? Its explanation is also hard to follow
Inflation-linked vs non-linked government bonds, 'coupon' and the interest tied to מק"מ are unclear; which is better now?
'Exposed to the dollar or hedged' is repeated but never explained
'A fund that tracks it' is unclear: what do I actually buy?
The general track gives no share range and leaves decisions to a committee, which worries the reader
Comprehensive vs general new pension fund and 'above the maximum amount' are unclear
The severance fund card leaves the reader unsure whether they have one
No mention of the tax benefit after age 60 for the investment savings fund
No information on whether money is protected if the bank or fund fails
No information on how fast, or at what cost, money can be withdrawn
No information on how much tax is paid on profit
Would drop the 'for children' section

problems.why: The reader asks whether מק"מ is a place money is held or an investment, since it appears in both roles; this is the person's point that it shouldn't be listed as a product.
